[Key Information from testbed/Canner__WrenAI-1890_2026-11-11_11-05-10/CONTRIBUTING.md]
- Environment Setup:
  - Use docker-compose to start all services, especially when contributing to multiple services.
  - Prepare `.env` file from `.env.example` in the `WrenAI/docker` folder:
    - `cd ../docker`
    - `cp .env.example .env.local`
    - Fill in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` with your key in `.env.local`.
  - Copy `config.example.yaml` to `config.yaml` in the same folder and update service URLs (e.g. change `http://wren-ui:3000` to `http://host.docker.internal:3000`).
  - Start services via docker-compose:
    - `docker-compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml --env-file .env.example up`
    - To run in background: add `-d` flag.
    - Stop with: `docker-compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml --env-file .env.example down`.
  - When contributing to multiple services, comment out services you start manually in `docker/docker-compose-dev.yml` and update `.env.local` accordingly.

- Project Structure & Contribution Scope:
  - Wren AI Service: LLM-related; converting natural language to SQL etc.
    - Contribution details in https://github.com/Canner/WrenAI/blob/main/wren-ai-service/CONTRIBUTING.md
  - Wren UI Service: Built with Next.js and TypeScript (client service).
    - Setup and running development server instructions in https://github.com/Canner/WrenAI/blob/main/wren-ui/README.md
  - Wren Engine Service: Semantic engine backend for LLMs.
    - Contributing guide at https://github.com/Canner/wren-engine/blob/main/ibis-server/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md
  - For multiple services:
    - Use docker-compose as above.
    - Adjust environment variables to point to manually started services.
    - Generally, start UI and Engine from source.

- Testing Instructions:
  - No explicit test commands or scripts mentioned in this file.
  - For the UI service, likely test commands are in its README.
  - No details for running individual or specific test files.
  - Overall testing strategy or commands not outlined in this document.

- Other relevant environment/configuration:
  - `.env.local` file required, derived from `.env.example`.
  - `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable required.
  - `config.yaml` for AI service configuration.

- Prerequisites:
  - Docker and docker-compose are required.
  - Node.js and TypeScript for Wren UI Service (implied as Next.js/TS used).
  - OpenAI API key needed (`OPENAI_API_KEY`).
